_purpose: Layer 3 of the eval: genes/programs whose cross-context (in vitro / in vivo / patient / mouse-human) behaviour is ALREADY documented in the literature. Each row's documented_verdict is ground truth for the persists/diverges/not_comparable logic — not for whether the pipeline can find the gene. Distinct from the 3 blinded behaviour cases (cases/) and from the synthetic classifier unit tests.
_how_to_use: Run each row's `human_symbol` through build_package in eval mode; hand the package + the row's context findings (as fixtures) to the agent; compare its verdict to documented_verdict.
Report agreement per bucket, not overall — a system that only ever says 'persists' scores 3/8 here and should look bad.
`pipeline_expectation` says what the deterministic package should contain for that gene; if it doesn't, that's a pipeline bug, not an agent failure — check it BEFORE grading the agent.
`confidence` is our confidence that the documented verdict is settled science. Rows marked `verify` need a teammate to read the cited paper's relevant figure before the row is used for grading.

verdict_vocabulary.persists: in-vitro finding is reproduced in vivo and in patients
verdict_vocabulary.partially_persists: direction holds but magnitude/isoform/maturity differs in a documented way
verdict_vocabulary.diverges: in-vitro finding is absent or reversed in vivo / patients, or the mouse and human patterns differ
verdict_vocabulary.not_comparable: the comparison cannot be made (no ortholog, no matched tissue, no matched patients)

rows.gene_or_program: FOS / JUN / JUNB / EGR1 immediate-early-gene program
rows.in_vitro_finding: Strongly induced in cells profiled by scRNA-seq after enzymatic dissociation at 37 °C; appears as a discrete 'stressed' cell state / subpopulation.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Absent when the same tissue is profiled without warm dissociation (snapshot in situ, snRNA-seq, or cold-active protease); the 'state' is a procedural artifact.
rows.patient_finding: Same artifact in human tumour and tissue scRNA-seq when collagenase-dissociated; not a disease state.
rows.verdict_note: Textbook artifact case. An agent that reports the IEG state as a biological finding that 'persists' fails.

sources.citation: van den Brink et al., Nat Methods 2017
O'Flanagan et al., Genome Biology 2019 (cold-active protease minimizes collagenase-associated stress response)
Denisenko et al., Genome Biology 2020 (dissociation/storage biases, sc vs sn)

rows.pipeline_expectation: mygene ok; orthology mouse one2one ok (Fos); GTEx shows broad expression (FOS is expressed everywhere, so GTEx alone cannot arbitrate — the agent must weigh the in-vivo fixture, not GTEx).

rows.in_vitro_finding: Induced by warm enzymatic dissociation alongside the IEG program; co-marks the artifactual 'stressed' cluster.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Not induced in intact tissue or under cold dissociation / nuclear isolation.
rows.patient_finding: Artifact reproduced in patient tissue when protocol is warm-enzymatic.
rows.verdict_note: Second artifact row so the 'diverges' bucket has two independent examples.

sources.citation: van den Brink et al., Nat Methods 2017

rows.pipeline_expectation: Note: HSPA1A/HSPA1B are near-identical paralogs; orthology to mouse Hspa1a/Hspa1b may come back one2many, so IMPC is `skipped` (no unique one2one). Good test that the agent treats `skipped` correctly.

rows.gene_or_program: MYH6 vs MYH7 myosin heavy-chain isoform ratio
rows.in_vitro_finding: hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes express a fetal-like isoform profile with relatively high MYH6; MYH7 rises with extended culture / maturation protocols but rarely reaches adult ratio.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Adult human ventricle is MYH7-dominant (MYH6 low). (Mouse is the opposite — adult mouse ventricle is Myh6-dominant — so the mouse axis is a divergence, see verdict_note.)
rows.patient_finding: Adult patient ventricular tissue MYH7-dominant; MYH6:MYH7 shift is itself a heart-failure readout.
rows.verdict_note: Direction of maturation holds, adult ratio does not. On the mouse↔human axis specifically the answer is `diverges` (Myh6-dominant adult mouse vs MYH7-dominant adult human) — a two-axis row; grade the axis the case asks about.

sources.citation: Guo & Pu, Cardiomyocyte Maturation, Circ Res 2020
Review, Stem Cell Res Ther 2023 (hiPSC-CM maturation)

rows.pipeline_expectation: GTEx: MYH7 high in Heart – Left Ventricle, low elsewhere; MYH6 highest in Heart – Atrial Appendage. Orthology mouse one2one ok. IMPC likely phenotyped (cardiac phenotypes).

rows.gene_or_program: TNNI1 → TNNI3 troponin I isoform switch
rows.in_vitro_finding: hiPSC-CMs predominantly express the fetal/slow-skeletal isoform TNNI1; TNNI3 (adult cardiac) is low and increases only with prolonged culture or maturation cues.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Adult heart is TNNI3-dominant; the TNNI1→TNNI3 switch is a standard maturation index.
rows.verdict_note: Same pattern as lit-03 but a different gene pair, so the bucket isn't carried by a single example.

sources.citation: Frontiers Bioeng Biotechnol 2026, transcriptome-based maturation assessment

rows.pipeline_expectation: GTEx: TNNI3 heart-restricted. Orthology one2one ok. IMPC Tnni3 likely phenotyped.

rows.gene_or_program: iPSC-derived cortical neuron identity — fetal rather than adult signature
rows.in_vitro_finding: iPSC-derived neurons express neuronal identity genes but their transcriptome (and 3D genome) most closely matches first/second-trimester fetal cortex; immature markers such as DCX remain high.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Adult cortex has low DCX and an adult (not fetal) layer/maturation signature.
rows.patient_finding: Adult patient post-mortem cortex: adult signature; iPSC models of adult-onset disease are therefore modelling a fetal-stage cell.
rows.verdict_note: Cell identity persists; maturation stage does not. A 'persists' verdict is wrong; 'diverges' is too strong.

sources.citation: Handel et al., Hum Mol Genet 2016 (similarity to primary tissue and cortical layer identity)
Fetal signatures in the 3D genome of iPSC-derived neurons, Genome Research 2026
Multi-site omics study of long-term iPSC-neuron differentiation, 2018

rows.pipeline_expectation: GTEx (adult tissue): DCX low in adult cortex — this is the one row where GTEx directly supports the verdict. Orthology one2one ok.

rows.in_vitro_finding: Expressed on all cultured/isolated haematopoietic cells; used as the gating marker.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Expressed on all nucleated haematopoietic cells in mouse (Ptprc) and human tissue atlases.
rows.patient_finding: Universal immune-compartment marker in patient tissue (Tabula Sapiens, HCA).
rows.verdict_note: Positive control. Any configuration should get this.

sources.citation: Shay et al., PNAS 2013 (conserved immune transcriptional programs mouse↔human)

rows.pipeline_expectation: All sources ok; GTEx highest in Whole Blood / Spleen / EBV lymphocytes; IMPC Ptprc phenotyped.

rows.in_vitro_finding: Expressed in epithelial lines and organoids; standard sorting marker.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Epithelial-restricted in mouse and human atlases.
rows.patient_finding: Epithelial-restricted in patient tissue; also used clinically (CTC capture).
rows.verdict_note: Second positive control, non-immune, so 'persists' isn't carried by one lineage.
rows.pipeline_expectation: GTEx high in colon/small intestine/kidney epithelium, ~0 in blood/brain; orthology one2one ok.

rows.gene_or_program: CXCL8 (IL-8) — human chemokine with no mouse ortholog
rows.in_vitro_finding: Strongly induced in human cells (epithelium, monocytes) by inflammatory stimuli.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Mouse has no CXCL8 gene; neutrophil chemotaxis is carried by Cxcl1/Cxcl2 (KC/MIP-2). There is nothing to compare to.
rows.patient_finding: Elevated in inflamed patient tissue/serum across many diseases (persists human in vitro → patient).
rows.verdict_note: Verdict is for the mouse↔human axis. This is the row that tests the pipeline's own status contract: orthology `not_found` is a database fact and must map to not_comparable, NOT to diverges and NOT to 'no evidence'. The human in-vitro→patient axis is `persists`.

sources.citation: Mestas & Hughes, J Immunol 2004, 'Of mice and not men'

rows.pipeline_expectation: ensembl_orthology.mus_musculus = `not_found`; rattus_norvegicus = `not_found`; macaca_mulatta = `ok`; IMPC = `skipped` (no unique one2one ortholog). This is exactly the package shape the agent must read correctly.

rows.in_vitro_finding: Mouse macrophages robustly induce Nos2 / nitric oxide on LPS+IFNγ; human monocyte-derived macrophages induce NOS2 weakly or inconsistently under the same in-vitro stimulation.
rows.in_vivo_finding: Orthologous gene, conserved sequence, but species-divergent regulation — the mouse in-vitro finding does not transfer to human cells.
rows.patient_finding: NOS2 protein detectable in some human inflammatory lesions but not the high-output NO response seen in mouse; a classic translational mismatch.
rows.verdict_note: Ortholog exists (unlike lit-08) but expression regulation differs — tests that the agent distinguishes 'comparable and different' from 'not comparable'.

sources.citation: Reconciling mouse and human immunology, Annu Rev Immunol

rows.pipeline_expectation: Orthology mouse one2one ok (Nos2); IMPC Nos2 phenotyped with immune hits; GTEx: low baseline everywhere (inducible gene) — agent must not read low GTEx as 'diverges' by itself.
rows.confidence: verify — the human-weak-induction claim is well cited in reviews but the magnitude is protocol-dependent; have a teammate confirm the specific figure you cite.

_pipeline_checks_doc: Machine-readable form of pipeline_expectation, consumed by bench/pipeline_bench.py (live packages) and bench/gen_fixtures.py (stub packages). mouse_orthology: expected status of sources.ensembl_orthology.mus_musculus (one2many = ok but no unique one2one). impc: expected status or 'any'. gtex_*: sanity checks on sources.gtex.data.tissues. gtex_tissues: values used ONLY when stubbing.
